items.title: 6.2 Arithmetic Progression or Arithmetic Sequence (A.P.) (Roman Urdu)

blocks.text: Pichle sabaq mein humne progressions ki teen qismein suni thin. Aaj pehli aur sab se aasan qism ki baari hai: arithmetic progression, jise mukhtasar A.P. kehte hain. Socheiye aap har hafte apne gullak mein 50 rupay daalte hain: 50, 100, 150, 200... Har baar barabar izafa. Yahi A.P. hai, aur iska formula aap poori zindagi istemal kar sakte hain.

A sequence \(\{a_{n}\}\) is an arithmetic sequence or arithmetic progression (A.P.) if \(a_{n} - a_{n-1}\) is the same number for all \(n \in \mathbb{N}\) and \(n > 1\). The difference \(a_{n} - a_{n-1}\) \((n > 1)\), i.e. the difference of two consecutive terms of an A.P., is called the common difference and is usually denoted by \(d\).

Yeh lambi definition asal mein ek seedhi si baat keh rahi hai: kisi bhi term mein se us se pichli term minus karein, jawab hamesha same aaye. Us same jawab ko common difference (mushtarik farq) kehte hain aur \(d\) se likhte hain. "\(n > 1\)" is liye likha hai ke pehli term se pehle koi term nahin, to \(a_{1} - a_{0}\) ka sawal hi paida nahin hota.
Yani arithmetic progression aisi sequence hai jis mein pehli term ke baad har term pichli term mein ek constant (fixed number) jama karne se milti hai. Yahi constant common difference kehlata hai.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.text: If \(a_{1}, a_{2}, a_{3}, \ldots, a_{n}, \ldots\) are in A.P., then \(d = a_{2} - a_{1} = a_{3} - a_{2} = \ldots\), where \(a_{n}\) is the \(n\)th term of the A.P.
Kitab ki misalein: neeche wali sequences A.P. hain.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
\(d\) kaise nikalein: kisi bhi term ko us se agli term mein se minus karein (baad wali minus pehle wali, ulta kabhi nahin).
(i) \(3 - 1 = 2\), \(5 - 3 = 2\), \(7 - 5 = 2\): har jagah same, to A.P. hai aur \(d = 2\).
(ii) \(51 - 54 = -3\), \(48 - 51 = -3\): same, to A.P. hai aur \(d = -3\). Kyun negative? Kyun ke terms ghat rahi hain. Negative \(d\) ka matlab hai neeche ki taraf chalti hui A.P.
Kisi sequence ko A.P. saabit karne ke liye yeh farq shuru se aakhir tak same hona chahiye. Ek jagah bhi farq badal jaye to A.P. nahin. Misal: \(2, 4, 8, \ldots\) ke farq \(2, 4\) hain, is liye yeh A.P. nahin (yeh geometric hai).
Ab dekhte hain ke \(n\) terms wali A.P. ki shakal kaisi hoti hai. Pehli term \(a_{1}\) hai, aur har qadam par \(d\) jama hota hai:

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab is jumle se pehle ek faltu '0' chhapti hai ('0An arithmetic progression...'). Sahi jumla hai: 'An arithmetic progression with \(n\) terms can be written as:'. Yeh sirf chhapai ki ghalti hai, maths par asar nahin.
Is liye arithmetic progression ki \(n\)th term ka formula yeh hai:

blocks.text_alt: a sub n equals a sub 1 plus (n minus 1) times d

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Sab se ahem sawal: \((n - 1)d\) kyun, \(nd\) kyun nahin? Qadam giniye. \(a_{1}\) se \(a_{2}\) tak \(d\) ek baar jama hota hai, \(a_{3}\) tak do baar, \(a_{4}\) tak teen baar. Yani \(a_{n}\) tak \(n - 1\) baar.
Rozmarra ki misaal: building ki pehli manzil se paanchvi manzil tak aap sirf 4 seedhiyan (staircases) chadhte hain, 5 nahin. Bilkul isi tarah.
Yeh formula chaar cheezon ko jorta hai: \(a_{n}\), \(a_{1}\), \(n\) aur \(d\). Koi teen maloom hon to chautha nikal sakte hain. A.P. ke zyada tar sawal bas yahi hain, is liye is formula ko achhi tarah samajh lijiye.

Formula ke chaar istemal ek nazar mein dekh lijiye, kyun ke exercise ke sawal inhi chaar shaklon mein aate hain:
1. \(a_{1}\), \(d\), \(n\) diye hon aur term chahiye: seedha rakhiye. Misaal: \(a_{1} = 2\), \(d = 5\), to \(a_{10} = 2 + 9(5) = 47\).
2. Term, \(a_{1}\), \(d\) diye hon aur \(n\) chahiye (yani "yeh kaun si term hai" ya "kitni terms hain"): equation bana kar \(n\) nikaaliye.
3. Term, \(a_{1}\), \(n\) diye hon aur \(d\) chahiye: \(d = \frac{a_{n} - a_{1}}{n - 1}\).
4. Do terms diye hon aur \(a_{1}\), \(d\) dono chahiye: do equations bana kar hal kijiye.
Har sawal mein pehle yeh pehchaniye ke chaar mein se kaun si cheez gum hai; phir raasta khud saaf ho jata hai.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.text:
(i) The 1st, 2nd, 3rd and \(n\)th terms of an A.P. are denoted by \(a_{1}\), \(a_{2}\), \(a_{3}\) and \(a_{n}\) respectively.
(ii) The \(n\)th term from the end of an A.P. is the \((m - n + 1)\)th term, where \(m\) denotes the total number of terms of the A.P.
(iii) Three numbers \(a, b, c\) are in A.P. if and only if \(2b = a + c\).
(iv) Any term (except the first and last) in an A.P. is equal to half of the sum of two terms equidistant from it.
(v) If the term \(a_{1}\) is unknown or not given, the \(n\)th term can be written as \(a_{n} = a_{m} + (n - m)d\) (the subscript of the given term and the coefficient of \(d\) sum to \(n\)).

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Ab in paanch baaton ko ek misaal se samajhte hain. A.P. lijiye \(3, 7, 11, \ldots, 39\), jis mein \(d = 4\) aur kul \(m = 10\) terms hain.
(ii) Aakhir se teesri term = shuru se \((10 - 3 + 1) = 8\)th term \(= 3 + 7(4) = 31\). Aakhir se ulta gin kar dekhiye: \(39, 35, 31\). Bilkul sahi. Kyun \(+1\)? Kyun ke aakhri term khud bhi ginti mein shamil hai: aakhir se pehli term \(m\)th hai, \(m - 1\)th nahin.
(iii) \(a, b, c\) A.P. mein hon to \(b - a = c - b\), yani \(2b = a + c\). Matlab beech wala number baqi do ka average hai. Misaal: \(3, 7, 11\) mein \(2(7) = 14 = 3 + 11\).
(iv) 5th term 19 hai; us se do do jagah door terms \(a_{3} = 11\) aur \(a_{7} = 27\) hain, aur \(\frac{11 + 27}{2} = 19\). Kyun? Ek taraf se \(2d\) kam, doosri taraf se \(2d\) zyada, dono jama karein to \(d\) cancel ho jata hai.
(v) Agar \(a_{1}\) maloom na ho magar koi aur term \(a_{m}\) maloom ho, to wahan se qadam ginein: \(a_{10} = a_{4} + (10 - 4)d = 15 + 6(4) = 39\). Subscript 4 aur coefficient 6 ka jama 10 hai, yahi kitab ki yaad dihani hai.

Note (iv) ka ek khoobsurat nateeja yeh hai ke A.P. mein shuru aur aakhir se barabar door terms ka jama hamesha same rehta hai: \(3 + 39 = 7 + 35 = 11 + 31 = 42\). Aage series (6.4) mein jama ka formula isi baat se banega, is liye isay abhi se zehan mein bitha lijiye. Isi wajah se middle term ki ahmiyat bhi hai: woh poori A.P. ka "markaz" hai.
Ab middle term (beech wali term). A.P. ki middle term is baat par munhasir hai ke terms kitni hain, maslan:

If the total number of terms of an A.P. is even, there are two middle terms, the \(\left(\frac{n}{2}\right)\)th and the \(\left(\frac{n}{2} + 1\right)\)th, where \(n\) is the number of terms. In example (i), 5 and 7 are the two middle terms.
If the total number of terms of an A.P. is odd, there is only one middle term, the \(\left(\frac{n+1}{2}\right)\)th term. In example (ii), 7 is the only middle term.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Yeh positions kyun? \(n = 6\) ke liye positions \(1, 2, \mathbf{3}, \mathbf{4}, 5, 6\) hain; koi akela beech nahin, is liye 3rd \(\left(\frac{6}{2}\right)\) aur 4th \(\left(\frac{6}{2} + 1\right)\) dono middle hain: \(a_{3} = 5\), \(a_{4} = 7\).
\(n = 7\) ke liye positions \(1, 2, 3, \mathbf{4}, 5, 6, 7\); 4th \(\left(\frac{7+1}{2}\right)\) term ke dono taraf teen teen terms hain, is liye sirf woh middle hai: \(a_{4} = 7\).
Jaise cricket team ke 11 khiladi line mein khade hon to 6th khiladi beech mein hoga: \(\frac{11 + 1}{2} = 6\).

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
1. \(10, 7, 4, 1, \ldots\) ka \(d\) kya hai? (Jawab: \(-3\).)
2. Kya \(5, 9, 13, 18\) A.P. hai? (Nahin: aakhri farq 5 hai, baqi 4.)
3. 9 terms wali A.P. ki middle term kaun si position par hai? (Jawab: \(\frac{9+1}{2} = 5\)th.)

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
(Yeh hamari practice hai, kitab ka sawal nahin.) A.P. \(54, 51, 48, \ldots\) ki 20th term nikaalein.
Given: \(a_{1} = 54\), \(d = 51 - 54 = -3\), \(n = 20\).
\[a_{20} = 54 + (20 - 1)(-3)\]
\[= 54 - 57 = -3\]
Kyun 19? Kyun ke 20th term tak 19 qadam hain. Jawab \(a_{20} = -3\).

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. A.P. mein lagataar terms ka farq hamesha same hota hai; yahi common difference \(d = a_{n} - a_{n-1}\) hai.
2. \(n\)th term: \(a_{n} = a_{1} + (n-1)d\).
3. \(a, b, c\) A.P. mein hain agar aur sirf agar \(2b = a + c\).
4. Aakhir se \(n\)th term = shuru se \((m - n + 1)\)th term (kul \(m\) terms).
5. \(a_{1}\) na ho to: \(a_{n} = a_{m} + (n - m)d\).
6. Middle term: \(n\) juft (even) ho to \(\frac{n}{2}\)th aur \(\left(\frac{n}{2} + 1\right)\)th; taaq (odd) ho to \(\frac{n+1}{2}\)th.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. \(a_{n} = a_{1} + nd\) likh dena: qadam \(n - 1\) hote hain. Bachne ka tareeqa: formula ko \(n = 1\) par check karein; \(a_{1} = a_{1} + 0\) aana chahiye.
2. Ulta minus karna: \(d = a_{2} - a_{1}\) hai. \(54, 51, 48\) mein \(d = -3\) hai, 3 nahin.
3. Sirf pehla farq dekh kar A.P. keh dena: saare farq check karein.
4. Middle term mein position aur value ko mila dena: \(n = 7\) mein middle position 4 hai, magar middle term us position ki value 7 hai.
